arguments.report:
# Runtime route registration → empty params / panic (gin @ /gin, commit 93ff80f)

## (a) Test output

Temp test `/gin/zz_repro_params_test.go`, run with `cd /gin && go test -run TestZZReproParams -v .`

**Exact reproduction from the bug report (route with `*wild`):**
```
=== RUN   TestZZReproParams
    zz_repro_params_test.go:15: first request status=404 (expected 404)
    zz_repro_params_test.go:23: after addRoute: engine.maxParams=3
--- FAIL: TestZZReproParams (0.00s)
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1] with capacity 0 [recovered]
	panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [:1] with capacity 0
github.com/gin-gonic/gin.(*node).getValue(...)
	/gin/tree.go:550 +0xdc5
github.com/gin-gonic/gin.(*Engine).handleHTTPRequest(...)
	/gin/gin.go:609 +0x1a8
github.com/gin-gonic/gin.(*Engine).ServeHTTP(...)
	/gin/gin.go:572 +0x1dd
```
So on this exact source the reported route **panics** (not 200) at `tree.go:550`. The panic is raised in `handleHTTPRequest` *before* `c.Next()`, so `Recovery` is not in the chain yet — I verified with `gin.Default()` that the panic escapes `ServeHTTP` too (no 500, the process/test panics).

**Same bug without a catch-all (`/test/:name/:last_name`) — this is the "200 with empty params" symptom:**
```
=== RUN   TestZZReproParamsNoWildcard
    first request status=404 (expected 404)
    after addRoute: engine.maxParams=2
    handler: name="" last_name="" (len(params)=0 cap=0)
    second request status=200
--- PASS: TestZZReproParamsNoWildcard
```
**Controls (both pass, proving the mechanism is the stale pooled Context):**
- route registered *before* the first request: `handler: name="john" last_name="smith" wild="/is/super/great" (cap=3)`, status 200.
- same order as the bug but pool re-created after `addRoute` (`router.pool = sync.Pool{New: func() any { return router.allocateContext() }}`): `name="john" last_name="smith" wild="/is/super/great" (cap=3)`, status 200.

## (b) Root cause — exact code path

1. `gin.go:566-575 Serv

arguments.text: Confirmed: in errors.go the `Unwrap()` method has a *pointer* receiver (`func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error`), while `Error()` has a value receiver. So a plain `Error` value implements `error` but exposes no chain to `errors.Is`/`errors.As`, which is why `fmt.Errorf("%w", err)` can't find `innerErr`. Fix: give `Unwrap` a value receiver (pointer values keep working, since *Error's method set includes value methods). Fixing now; ETA ~7 min.

Confirmed: `responseWriter.WriteHeader` logs the "[WARNING] Headers were already written" message but then falls through and still assigns `w.status = code`, so `Status()` reports a code that was never sent. Fix: return early in that branch so the already-sent status is preserved. Fixing now; ETA ~7 min.

Confirmed and reproduced. Root cause: contexts are pooled and their `params` slice is pre-allocated with capacity `engine.maxParams` at allocation time. Your first request (404, before any route) creates a context with capacity 0, which goes back into the pool. Registering the route later raises `maxParams`, but the pooled context keeps its capacity-0 slice, and `node.getValue` only fills params "within preallocated capacity" (`if params != nil && cap(*params) > 0`), so every param is dropped; the catch-all branch has no such guard and actually panics with "slice bounds out of range [:1] with capacity 0". Fix: make `getValue` grow the params (and skippedNodes) slices instead of silently dropping/panicking. Fixing now; ETA ~8 min.

arguments.text: Confirmed: in tree.go's `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` (used by RedirectFixedPath) the code descends with `n = n.children[0]` and then switches on the node type, assuming the wildcard child is first — but wildcard children are always stored LAST (`addChild` inserts static children before the wildcard, and getValue uses `children[len(children)-1]`). So for a node with both `/prefix/xxx` and `/prefix/:id`, children[0] is the static node and the switch hits `default: panic("invalid node type")`. Fixing: use the last child, and try static children case-insensitively first (so /PREFIX/XXX resolves to /prefix/xxx) with the wildcard only as fallback (so /prefix/a/b/c 404s). ETA ~5 min.

Confirmed: `NegotiateFormat` iterates `for ; i < len(accepted); i++` but indexes `offer[i]` too, so when the Accept entry is longer than the offered format (e.g. accepted "image/tiff-fx" vs offer "image/tiff") it indexes past the end of the offer → `index out of range [10] with length 10`. Fix: bound the loop by the offer length as well, so a longer Accept entry simply doesn't match and "" is returned. ETA ~5 min.

Confirmed: `Context.FileAttachment` writes the ASCII filename into `Content-Disposition` verbatim (`attachment; filename="`+filename+`"`), so embedded `"`/`\` break out of the quoted string and inject extra header parameters. Fix: escape `\` and `"` in the filename (the same escaping net/http uses) so the header always holds exactly one well-formed filename. ETA ~5 min.
